digest.component_or_area: bridge status durable state and canary consumption
propositions: Replace duplicate pass-record producers with one process-finalizer writer that records authoritative JSON to refs/reconciler/last-pass before releasing refs/reconciler/lock, using three-attempt CAS with 100/200ms backoff on observed-OID mismatch.

Canonical rebar bridge status and hidden alias bridge-status use identical parser, core, options, output formats, and errors, exposing read-only fast snapshots with total precedence PAUSED > RUNNING > FOREIGN > FAILED > STALE > HEALTHY and appropriate exit codes.

Local writer and status derive stable identity from explicit REBAR_ENV_ID or local:<repo-env-id> from .env-id, treating missing/empty/unreadable .env-id as hard configuration error, while inbound event metadata and LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID remain unchanged.

Canary moves from GitHub Actions heartbeat polling to durable git state by fetching refs/reconciler/*, defaulting to status source, performing two read-only live-lock snapshots to detect CRASHED state, and preserving explicit github-api rollback for one release.

Rich detail file .tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/last-pass.json is single-writer rolling state that safely degrades when absent or mismatched; status includes detail only when pass and environment ids match the authoritative ref.

Stalled fence (unchanged OID/fence across two snapshots within observed lease) is witnessed as canary-only CRASHED result, while SIGKILL/OOM/runner teardown are never invented in last-pass; lease over 480s is rejected immediately against fixed 10-minute budget.
